title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: The bulk narrowing rewrote a protected open member into a private open one, which Kotlin rejects, and a real project stopped compiling.

highlights.title: A member that can be overridden stays visible
highlights.description: Kotlin refuses private open and private abstract, since a private member cannot be overridden. Those members are left alone rather than rewritten.

highlights.title: Refusing beats dropping the keyword
highlights.description: Removing the open instead would change what subclasses outside the workspace can do, and the detector only proves that nothing inside it uses the member.

highlights.title: One rule, four producers
highlights.description: The rule against deleting and editing the same URI held at one of its four call sites. A witness now exercises each of them.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A member carrying open, abstract or sealed is never narrowed to private.
The enum entry removal plans its cascade before writing, like the other three.
